faq.q: Where did the first humans come from?
faq.a: Our species, Homo sapiens, first appeared in Africa about 300,000 years ago. The oldest known bones were found at Jebel Irhoud in Morocco.

faq.q: Why did early humans leave Africa?
faq.a: Nobody kept a diary, so we use clues. Most likely small groups followed animals, food and water, and changes in climate opened new paths. Each generation moved only a little.

faq.q: How did people get to Australia?
faq.a: Australia was never joined to Asia by land, even in the Ice Age, so the first people crossed open sea, probably on rafts or boats, at least 50,000 years ago.
asks: How did the first Australians arrive?

faq.a: Yes. Neanderthals already lived in Europe and western Asia. The two groups met and sometimes had children together, so many people today carry a little Neanderthal DNA.

faq.q: How do we know when people arrived?
faq.a: Scientists date bones, tools, campfires and cave paintings, using methods like radiocarbon dating. They also compare the DNA of people around the world today.
asks: How do scientists date early humans?

facts: The oldest known Homo sapiens fossils, from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, are about 300,000 years old.
A cave painting on Sulawesi in Indonesia has been dated to at least 51,200 years ago.
People reached Australia at least 50,000 years ago, crossing open sea.

quiz.say: Which continent did all modern humans first come from?
quiz.show: Where did Homo sapiens first appear?
quiz.why: The oldest bones of our species, about 300,000 years old, come from Africa.

wrong.1: People reached Europe much later, around 45,000 years ago.
wrong.2: Australia was reached by boat 50,000 or more years ago, long after.

quiz.say: How did the first people reach Australia?
quiz.show: How did people first reach Australia?
quiz.why: There was always open sea between Asia and Australia, so people must have crossed it on boats or rafts.

wrong.1: Even when sea levels were low, a stretch of open sea remained.
wrong.2: Horses were tamed tens of thousands of years later.
